questions.stem: The festival of 'Baisakhi' (Vaisakhi), observed every year on April 13 or 14, marks which founding event in Sikh religious history?

options.option_text: Martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur at Chandni Chowk, Delhi in 1675
Installation of the Adi Granth at Harmandir Sahib by Guru Arjan Dev
Establishment of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699
Birth of Guru Nanak Dev Ji at Rai Bhoi di Talvandi, Punjab

questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa Panth on Baisakhi day (March 30, 1699) at Anandpur Sahib — this is the Sikh significance of Baisakhi. Option A (Guru Tegh Bahadur's martyrdom) occurred in November 1675 and is not linked to Baisakhi. Baisakhi is also a harvest festival for Punjabis in general, but its specifically Sikh observance commemorates the Khalsa founding.

questions.stem: 'Chapchar Kut', celebrated after completion of jungle clearing for jhum (shifting) cultivation, is the spring festival of which northeastern state?

options.option_text: Mizoram, celebrated in February–March by the Mizo people
Nagaland, observed alongside its November tribal festival season
Manipur, observed by the Meitei community in the Imphal Valley
Meghalaya, celebrated by the Khasi and Garo hill communities

questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut is exclusively a Mizo festival of Mizoram, held in February–March after jhum land clearing; it features the traditional Cheraw (bamboo) dance. Option B is wrong because Nagaland's signature festival is Hornbill (November), unconnected to jhum clearing. Option C is wrong as Manipur's spring festival is Yaoshang, a separate tradition of the Meitei community.

questions.stem: 'Thrissur Pooram', described as the 'mother of all Poorams' and famous for the grandest display of caparisoned elephants and percussion ensembles in Kerala, is centered at which temple?

options.option_text: Padmanabhaswamy Temple, the Vishnu shrine in Thiruvananthapuram
Guruvayur Sri Krishna Temple in Guruvayur, Thrissur district
Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple in the Pathanamthitta hill forests
Vadakkumnathan Temple in Thrissur, the ancient Shiva shrine

questions.explanation: Thrissur Pooram is held at Vadakkumnathan Temple (a Shiva temple) in Thrissur city; two temple groups — Thiruvambady and Paramekkavu — converge there with elephants and fireworks. Option B (Guruvayur) is the most tempting distractor as it also lies in Thrissur district, but Guruvayur Temple's celebrated occasion is Guruvayur Ekadashi, not Thrissur Pooram.

questions.stem: The 'Yaoshang' festival, celebrated over five days during the full moon of Lamta (February–March), features 'Thabal Chongba' — a moonlit folk dance performed by youth in hand-holding circles. This festival is the largest annual celebration of which northeastern state?

options.option_text: Mizoram, where Chapchar Kut is the comparable spring harvest event
Manipur, where it is the biggest festival of the Meitei community
Tripura, celebrated by the Kokborok-speaking tribal communities
Assam, where Rongali Bihu is the comparable spring festival season

questions.explanation: Yaoshang is Manipur's biggest festival, coinciding with the Holi season; it includes puja and the Thabal Chongba folk dance of Meitei youth. Option D (Assam's Rongali Bihu) is a tempting distractor because it also falls in spring, but Bihu has a completely distinct dance form and cultural tradition unrelated to Thabal Chongba or Yaoshang rituals.

questions.stem: In South India, the eve of Holi is observed as 'Kama Dahanam,' where an effigy is ritually burned. Which mythological episode does this practice specifically commemorate?

options.option_text: Holika entering the pyre with devotee Prahlada to harm the child
Shiva incinerating Kamadeva (god of love) with fire from his third eye
Narasimha (Vishnu's avatar) slaying the demon king Hiranyakashipu
Goddess Kali vanquishing the demon Raktabija on a moonlit battlefield

questions.explanation: Kama Dahanam commemorates Shiva burning Kamadeva to ashes with his third eye when Kamadeva shot a love-arrow to break Shiva's penance. This is distinct from the North Indian Holika Dahan (Option A), which re-enacts Prahlada's miraculous survival — both are bonfire traditions on the same night but reference entirely different mythological narratives.

questions.stem: 'Ali Aye Ligang', a seed-sowing festival celebrated in February, features the 'Ponung' dance performed exclusively by women. This festival belongs to which specific tribe of Arunachal Pradesh?

options.option_text: Apatani tribe of the Ziro valley, Lower Subansiri district
Nyishi tribe of Kurung Kumey and East Kameng districts
Adi tribe of the Siang river valley, Arunachal Pradesh
Wancho tribe of Longding district, eastern Arunachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: Ali Aye Ligang ('Ali' = seeds/roots, 'Aye' = fruits, 'Ligang' = sowing festival) is the principal festival of the Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh; the Ponung dance performed exclusively by Adi women is its hallmark. Option A (Apatani) is a common distractor because Apatanis are also renowned agriculturists in Ziro, but their festivals include Myoko and Dree — not Ali Aye Ligang.

questions.stem: 'Nuakhai Juhar', the principal harvest festival of western Odisha, involves offering the first grain of the new crop to a presiding goddess before the community partakes. Which deity receives this first 'Nua' (new food) offering?

options.option_text: Goddess Samaleswari of Sambalpur, the presiding deity of western Odisha
Lord Jagannath of Puri, the paramount state deity of entire Odisha
Goddess Maa Tarini, worshipped as Shakti across the Ganjam district
Goddess Stambheshwari of Binka in the Subarnapur district, Odisha

questions.explanation: Nuakhai originates in the Sambalpur region; the first grain is ceremonially offered to Goddess Samaleswari (the presiding deity of Sambalpur) before the community celebrates. Option B (Jagannath) is the most tempting distractor because Jagannath is Odisha's state deity, but the Nuakhai ritual is locally tied to Samaleswari — Jagannath receives a separate Nua offering only in the Puri region, not as the primary Nuakhai tradition.
